n: Once, when Ephraim spoke, others trembled—it was the leading tribe. But when it became guilty through Baal worship, it “died” spiritually and politically.

f.w: he exalted himself in Israel
when he offended in Baal, he died

n: They keep sinning more and more, making metal idols by their own design. People even say, “Let those who sacrifice kiss the calves!”—humans kissing idols in worship.

f.w: molten images
f.g: Idols made from melted, cast metal.

f.w: kiss the calves
f.g: Kissing an idol was an act of worship.

n: So they will vanish like morning mist, early dew, chaff blown from a threshing floor, or smoke from a window. Four images of things that disappear quickly.

f.w: as the morning cloud
as the chaff
chimney
f.g: A window or opening that let smoke out.

n: “I am the LORD your God since Egypt; you know no God but Me, and there is no Savior except Me.” Latter-day Saints understand this Savior, Jehovah, to be Jesus Christ.

f.w: there is no saviour beside me

n: God cared for them in the desert, a land of terrible drought.

f.w: I did know thee in the wilderness

n: When they had good pasture, they were satisfied; when satisfied, they became proud and forgot God—a cycle repeated throughout scripture, and called the “pride cycle” in the Book of Mormon.

f.w: their heart was exalted; therefore have they forgotten me

n: So God will be like a lion and a leopard lurking beside the road.

f.w: I will be unto them as a lion

n: Like a bear robbed of her cubs, He will tear them open. The fierce images show how serious covenant betrayal is.

f.w: a bear that is bereaved of her whelps
caul

n: “O Israel, you have destroyed yourself; but in Me is your help.” Their ruin is self-inflicted; their only rescue is God.

f.w: thou hast destroyed thyself; but in me is thine help

n: Where is your king now to save you? Where are the rulers you demanded? God offers Himself as their true King.

f.w: Give me a king and princes
I will be thy king
f.g: Many translations read “Where now is your king?”

n: God gave them a king in anger—beginning with Saul—and took kings away in wrath. Their last king, Hoshea, was captured by Assyria.

f.w: I gave thee a king in mine anger

n: Ephraim’s guilt is wrapped up and stored away, kept on record like a document tied and sealed. It will not be forgotten.

f.w: bound up
f.g: Tied up and preserved, like a sealed document.

n: Labor pains have come for rebirth, but Ephraim is an unwise child who won’t come out of the womb when it’s time. The nation refuses the new birth repentance offers.

f.w: The sorrows of a travailing woman
he should not stay long in the place of the breaking forth of children
f.g: He doesn’t present himself at the moment of birth.

n: A sudden burst of hope: “I will ransom them from the grave and redeem them from death. O death, where are your plagues? O grave, where is your sting?” Paul quoted this as a triumph song of Christ’s resurrection.

f.w: I will ransom them from the power of the grave
O death, I will be thy plagues
repentance shall be hid from mine eyes
f.g: Possibly “compassion is hidden from My eyes”—the Hebrew is debated.

n: Though Ephraim (“fruitful”) thrives among his brothers, a scorching east wind from the Lord will dry up his springs. The plunderer will take all his treasures—Assyria, sweeping in from the east.

f.w: an east wind shall come
f.g: The hot desert wind—an image of Assyria.

n: Samaria will bear its guilt for rebelling against God, and suffer the horrors of ancient war. Samaria fell to Assyria in 722 BC after a three-year siege.

f.w: Samaria shall become desolate
